clue.text: Stuff openly woven by wizard in combat

parts.note: scrim is a loosely woven fabric used in theatres and upholstery
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: Someone describes loose-weave cloth being worked by a sorcerer in the middle of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrimmage is a confused, disorderly fight or tussle, a synonym for combat.

parts.note: Sat is the standard abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: A remark about the one day, or perhaps the year, that belongs to a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology a satyr is a goat-like woodland god given to lust, so the word is used for any lustful man.

indicators.note: whisking stirs things up vigorously, so the letters of the two words beside it are mixed

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: whip this up to make imitation cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whisking' and 'cream' make a convincing kitchen scene, but the cream is a share skimmed off the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream taken off a deal is the profitable portion someone skims, which is what a rake-off is.

definitions.meaning: ..., or musth, is the periodic state of frenzied aggression in bull elephants
a ... is something essential, as in 'this book is a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an elephant's frenzied state and something one simply has to have.

indicators.note: other signals a different form of the word each, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people wound one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurt each other' reads as a phrase; 'other' is the anagram signal working on 'each'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt or be painful, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: It's under way as two men bat together with Kent's opening spell

indicators.note: together suggests the pieces are thrown in with one another and mixed
a spell is a charm that transforms, so the pooled letters are changed into a new order
two asks for the word men to be written twice

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: two batsmen at the crease together, with Kent opening the batting.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN twice, BAT and K are mixed together to give the answer. 'It's under way' is the definition: an embankment is what lies under a raised road or railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An embankment is a raised bank of earth carrying a road or railway, so it sits beneath the way.

clue.text: It has bill as introduction to throat

indicators.note: the bill is introduced into the throat, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: maw is an old word for the throat or gullet
ac is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Something comes with an invoice as a preface to a sore throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like the invoice, giving AC (account); the definition reads it as a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large parrot, a bird with a big hooked bill.

clue.text: Invited British entrant to walk in party

indicators.note: an entrant goes into something, so these letters are put inside the walk

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered public walk, as in Pall Mall
asked means invited

explanation.surface: A British person who has been invited enters a stroll during a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A masked ball is a dance party at which the guests wear masks.

clue.text: Sailing vessel gets line in mess

indicators.note: in tells us the line goes inside the sailing vessel

parts.note: a cutter is a single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A yacht has a rope tangled up in some untidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutter is an untidy mass of things, a synonym for mess.

clue.text: Married to conceal broken hearts — that's the point of separation

indicators.note: concealing something holds it inside, so the married word wraps the other letters

parts.note: wed means married

indicators.note: broken hearts are shattered, so the letters of hearts are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wedlock hides heartbreak, and that is where couples part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals an anagram of the six letters of the heart word, and 'to conceal' puts that scramble inside the married word. The surface's heartbreak in marriage misleads toward divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is the ridge dividing river basins, hence a turning point or dividing line.

definitions.meaning: read literally, to take the biscuit is to get a cracker
the idiom 'that ...' means that beats everything

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so outrageous it outdoes everything else, and literally means grabbing a cracker.

definitions.meaning: a crow, a bird that flies
to swindle them, to fleece them

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a crow-family bird and a verb meaning to cheat someone out of money.

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put up before the deal
ter is an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: An animal marks out land as its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteater is an animal, a creature that feeds on ants and termites.

clue.text: It's backing horse to muddle through most of the way

indicators.note: the muddle runs through the shortened road, so it goes inside
most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: a street is a way or road
to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: Someone bets on a horse to stumble its way down most of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the road's last letter and 'through' sets the muddle inside it. 'It's backing horse' looks like a punter's bet; it is the frame on a horse's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddletree is the frame of a saddle, which sits on and backs onto a horse's back.

parts.note: read as a bedroom item whose work is to contain down feathers, not someone keeping employment

explanation.definitionFit: A cover for a cushion on a bed holds the down filling inside, so holding down is its function.

clue.text: Act in belief in God's negative disposition

indicators.note: in tells us the act goes inside the belief

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator God based on reason
a feat is an act or deed

explanation.surface: A deed done in faith reveals a pessimistic outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the habit of expecting or accepting failure, a pessimistic negative attitude.

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a German is a European

explanation.surface: Track a fishing vessel from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a dogger is a Dutch two-masted fishing boat, and the answer is a crewman from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries list the word with the dogger, a Dutch two-masted fishing vessel, as one who sails in it.

clue.text: Talking bunk is sort of right

indicators.note: talking means the word is spoken, so we want something sounding like it

parts.note: a berth is a bunk on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Spoken rubbish counts as a kind of correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like nonsense, but here it is a bed. The definition plays on birthright: birth is one kind of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth gives a birthright, so the word is a kind of right in the compound sense.

indicators.note: spinning turns the abbreviation round so it is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a spinning top is chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary word meaning icy or very cold.

clue.text: Perhaps spill vessel to make it so

definitions.meaning: a spill is a taper of wood or paper used for lighting a fire, one kind of igniter
a flat-bottomed barge takes cargo off a ship and so reduces its weight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a device for igniting, and a barge used to unload ships so they weigh less.

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doll gets restyled so that it endures.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-lived endures for a long time, so it is lasting.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns up the control on some measuring scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places REIN above REV in this down clue; 'up' then reads the whole column backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernier is a small sliding auxiliary scale for reading fine measurements.

clue.text: Birdie that's bettered by one wiseacre

parts.note: in golf a birdie is one under par and an eagle two under, so an eagle beats it by one stroke
an owl is proverbially wise, and a solemn know-all may be called an owl

explanation.surface: A golfer's birdie is outdone by one shot from a clever-clogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdie' looks like golf, but it defines a bird; it also supplies the golf context in which the eagle beats the birdie by one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle owl is a very large owl, and birdie is a playful word for a bird.

definitions.meaning: a gentle is an angler's word for a maggot used as bait

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a larva like an angler's maggot and the verb for digging about in earth.

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Bar a student from renting an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means dull and unoriginal, which is the figurative sense of flat.

clue.text: Where a crop may be scaled

definitions.text: Where a crop may be scaled

parts.words: Where a crop may be scaled
parts.note: read as a place where the harvest has scales, being reared aquatic animals, not a crop climbed or weighed

explanation.definitionFit: Aquaculture sites raise salmon or trout as a crop, and those creatures have scales.

indicators.note: to resolve is to break down and reform, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone launches a firm ethical commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: A materialisation is the appearance of something, such as a ghost taking bodily form.

clue.text: Tongue right in the middle of face

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right goes inside

parts.note: the nose sits at the centre of the face

explanation.surface: Someone sticks out their tongue right in the middle of someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is the language of medieval Scandinavia, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Record "Hot Rock" is cut very short

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: a cut word loses its last letter

parts.note: an emerald is a gemstone, informally a rock

explanation.surface: A record called Hot Rock gets edited down drastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, fleeting.
